findings.issue_text: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:70-81`, `addGuests.schema.ts:3-6`
**Blacklist bypass by casing** — the list is lowercased, `guest` is not. `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS=spam@evil.com` is defeated by `Spam@Evil.com`.
**Blacklist bypass by whitespace** — no `.trim()` after `.split(",")`. The natural `"a@x.com, b@x.com"` yields a dead `" b@x.com"` entry that can never match.

**`uniqueGuests` is not unique** — it filters against *existing* attendees but never against itself. `["a@b.com","a@b.com"]` passes both, `createMany` (line 101) writes two identical rows, and the guest gets two confirmation emails. Same across casings.
The uniqueness check exists **only on the client** (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29`); a tRPC mutation is a public API boundary. `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` has no `.refine()` and no `.max()`.
`_router.tsx:78`, `addGuests.handler.ts:52-56`, `addGuests.schema.ts:4`

**I1. `isTeamAdminOrOwner` uses `&&` where the name and intent say `||`; team admins locked out** — `addGuests.handler.ts:46-48`. In cal.com `isTeamAdmin` is satisfied by ADMIN *or* OWNER and `isTeamOwner` only by OWNER (unverifiable here), making this equivalent to `isTeamOwner` alone. Every team ADMIN gets `FORBIDDEN`. Also `teamId ?? 0` passes a sentinel into two DB queries for every personal booking, and the awaits are needlessly sequential.

**I2. Uses `authedProcedure` instead of `bookingsProcedure`** — `_router.tsx:78`. The directly adjacent `editLocation` (line 62), the closest analogue, uses `bookingsProcedure`, which exists to centralize the booking-ownership check. Hand-rolling it is how I1 and C2 got in; future hardening of the shared guard won't apply here.

**I3. No booking status or time guard** — `addGuests.handler.ts:26-56`, `BookingListItem.tsx:554`. The handler never reads `booking.status` or `endTime`. Adding a guest to a CANCELLED/REJECTED booking succeeds and sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` ("confirmed") with an ICS carrying `status: "CONFIRMED"`. And the UI offers the action on **past** bookings — `bookedActions` now contains the item (lines 193-200) and renders at line 554 under `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed`.

**I4. `sendAddGuestsEmails` is the only sender in `email-manager.ts` that ignores event-type email-disable settings** — `email-manager.ts:525-549`. Every other sender, including `sendLocationChangeEmails` immediately above (495-524), gates on `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (lines 99, 111, 140, 158, 176, 194, 206, 227, 248, 260, 287, 301, 322, 358…). This one takes no `eventTypeMetadata` at all. Customers who disabled cal.com transactional email will silently start receiving it again.

**I5. The team-member notification loop is dead code** — `email-manager.ts:531-537` iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members`, but the only caller builds `evt` (`handler:124-147`) without a `team` property. Team co-hosts are never notified; `organizer-add-guests-email.ts:22` always falls through to the organizer name.

**I6. `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes raw input instead of `uniqueGuests`** — `handler:168`. `newGuests` drives the new-vs-existing branch at `email-manager.ts:540`, so an address filtered out for *already being an attendee* is still classed as new and gets a duplicate "your booking is confirmed."

**I10. Seated event types unhandled** — `handler:92-106, 145-146`. `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` are copied onto `evt`, so seats were on the author's mind, but the write creates plain attendee rows with no `BookingSeat` reference and no limit check — over-filling the slot and producing attendees the seats-aware cancel flow can't address by `seatReferenceUid` (cf. `BookingListItem.tsx:135-138`). Cal.com's own copy says seats "automatically disables guest & opt-in bookings" (`common.json:1052`).

**I12. `you_do_not_have_permission` is not a real translation key** — `handler:55`, `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45`. No such key in `common.json`; the nearest is `dont_have_permission` (line 1628). The client renders `t(err.message)` directly, so users see the literal toast **"FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission"**. Two more bugs in the same handler: a template literal is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code and the `unable_to_add_guests` string added by this PR (`common.json:1137`) is never used; and prefixing toasts with the raw TRPC code (`undefined:` when `err.data` is absent) leaks internals.

`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` — validation schema duplicated client-side and rebuilt every render; shadows the server schema's name with a different shape; its `.refine()` is exactly what the server is missing (C1).
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33, 36-41` — `isInvalidEmail` never reset on success or `onOpenChange`; reopen the dialog and the red banner is still there. Only Cancel (line 90) clears it.
`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51` — if the user removes every row, `length === 0` returns silently with no feedback.
`handler:26` — `findFirst` on a unique primary key; should be `findUnique`.
`handler:58-61` — `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` throws a raw Prisma `P2025` (unhandled 500) for null-`userId` bookings instead of a typed TRPC error.
`handler:80-81` — if every address was dropped by the *blacklist*, the user is told "emails must be unique and valid"; partial blacklist drops are silent.
`BookingListItem.tsx:194`, `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:93` — `id`/`data-testid` of `add_members`; these are guests, and "members" means team members elsewhere. Rename before tests depend on it.
`handler:173` — `return { message: "Guests added" }` is hardcoded English and the client ignores it entirely.

`packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2` — imports from its own package barrel `@calcom/ui` while `index.tsx:153` re-exports it. `dynamic()` saves it from a module-eval cycle, but it pulls the whole UI barrel into the chunk, defeating the lazy split.
`MultiEmail.tsx:11` reassigns the `value` prop; `:19` uses `key={index}` on a removable list (focus jumps); `:35` sets `required` with no enclosing `<form>`.

`handler:124-147` — sparse `CalendarEvent`: no `bookerUrl`, `additionalNotes`, `customInputs`, `responses`, `eventTypeId`. New guests get a confirmation missing the booking questions everyone else's copy shows; `bookerUrl`-derived links may emit `undefined/...`.
`handler:138` — recurring: `recurringEvent` is set on `evt` but only one occurrence is modified. UI hides the action on the recurring tab (`BookingListItem.tsx:246`); the API does not.
`BookingListItem.tsx:357-361` — `AddGuestsDialog` mounted per row. Consistent with existing dialogs, so pre-existing, but compounding.
**Scope vs. title:** "guest *management*" but only add is implemented — no list, edit, or remove. Per C2, no remove means no way to undo an abusive add.

The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts, BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is parsed with `split(",")` and only lowercased: `split(",").map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`. If the env var is formatted naturally with spaces (e.g. "a@x.com, b@x.com"), the second entry becomes " b@x.com" (leading space) and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` will not match a guest email "b@x.com". adjudication_records.issue_text: The uniqueness check exists **only on the client** (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29`); a tRPC mutation is a public API boundary. `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` has no `.refine()` and no `.max()`.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the diff, the client dialog defines a Zod schema with a `.refine()` to enforce uniqueness (`AddGuestsDialog.tsx`), but the server-side tRPC input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint (and no size limit). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `guests.filter(...)` but it only filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails; it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. That means an attacker (or buggy client) can submit duplicate emails and the handler will pass them through to `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows or causing a DB error depending on constraints. So the finding about uniqueness being enforced only on the client is a real, verifiable issue in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts) explicitly tries to notify `calendarEvent.team?.members` via a loop. However, the only added caller is `addGuestsHandler`, which constructs `evt: CalendarEvent` without setting any `team` property (it sets `organizer`, `attendees`, `destinationCalendar`, etc., but no `team`). Since `sendAddGuestsEmails` immediately runs `const calendarEvent = formatCalEvent(calEvent);` and then checks `if (calendarEvent.team?.members)`, that branch will never execute for this caller unless `formatCalEvent` somehow injects `team` data (not shown in the diff). As introduced, the team-member notification path is therefore effectively unreachable for the new add-guests flow, so team co-hosts/admin members won’t be notified by this new feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I10. Seated event types unhandled** — `handler:92-106, 145-146`. `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` are copied onto `evt`, so seats were on the author's mind, but the write creates plain attendee rows with no `BookingSeat` reference and no limit check — over-filling the slot and producing attendees the seats-aware cancel flow can't address by `seatReferenceUid` (cf. `BookingListItem.tsx:135-138`). adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` always appends rows via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` with no conditional logic for seated events and no capacity check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot`. It also does not create any seat-specific entity/reference (it only creates plain `attendees` records), yet it explicitly copies `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` onto the `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) which indicates seat-aware behavior exists elsewhere. Additionally, the UI action to open `AddGuestsDialog` is added unconditionally in `BookingListItem.tsx`, so seated bookings would expose this flow. This makes overfilling and incompatibility with seat-aware flows a real risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **I12. `you_do_not_have_permission` is not a real translation key** — `handler:55`, `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:42-45`. No such key in `common.json`; the nearest is `dont_have_permission` (line 1628). The client renders `t(err.message)` directly, so users see the literal toast **"FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission"**. Two more bugs in the same handler: a template literal is always truthy, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` is dead code and the `unable_to_add_guests` string added by this PR (`common.json:1137`) is never used; and prefixing toasts with the raw TRPC code (`undefined:` when `err.data` is absent) leaks internals.

adjudication.rationale: The toast error handling in `AddGuestsDialog` is verifiably flawed: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` always produces a (truthy) string (e.g., `"undefined: ..."`), so `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), ...)` can never hit the fallback and will also surface `undefined:` when `err.data?.code` is missing. This is a real correctness/UI defect introduced by the diff and does leak internal error codes into user-facing UI. The specific claim that `you_do_not_have_permission` is not a translation key is plausible (the diff doesn’t add it while the handler throws that message), but it’s not fully provable from the provided `common.json` excerpt alone; however, the toast-construction bugs are definitively present in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26-29` — validation schema duplicated client-side and rebuilt every render; shadows the server schema's name with a different shape; its `.refine()` is exactly what the server is missing (C1).

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the Zod schema is indeed created inside the component (so it’s rebuilt each render) and it validates only the `string[]` email list, not the server’s `{ bookingId, guests }` object shape. However, it does not “shadow” the server schema in any technical sense (it’s a different module with a local constant; no import/name collision). Also, rebuilding a small Zod schema each render is at most a minor perf/maintainability nit, not a clear bug/correctness defect on its own. While the server schema lacks a uniqueness constraint, that issue is not caused by the client schema definition and the proposed finding as written is not a precise, verifiable defect in the diff at those lines.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:33, 36-41` — `isInvalidEmail` never reset on success or `onOpenChange`; reopen the dialog and the red banner is still there. Only Cancel (line 90) clears it.

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` when validation fails (`handleAdd` else-branch), but it is only cleared in the Cancel button handler. The `onSuccess` callback resets `multiEmailValue` and closes the dialog, but does not call `setIsInvalidEmail(false)`. Also, `Dialog`’s `onOpenChange` is wired directly to `setIsOpenDialog` with no state reset. So if the user triggers the error banner, closes the dialog via ESC/click-outside (or even succeeds afterward), reopening can still show the red banner because `isInvalidEmail` remains `true` in state.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49-51` — if the user removes every row, `length === 0` returns silently with no feedback.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`, `handleAdd` contains `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) { return; }` with no toast, error state, or UI feedback. Since `MultiEmail` lets users remove rows (it splices the array), the user can end up with `multiEmailValue = []` and still has access to the dialog's "Add" button. Clicking "Add" in that state will do nothing visibly, so the finding describes a real, verifiable UX/correctness issue introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:26` — `findFirst` on a unique primary key; should be `findUnique`.

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the code uses `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId }, ... })`. While `id` is typically a unique primary key and `findUnique` would be more idiomatic, `findFirst` with an `id` filter still returns the correct record (or null) and does not introduce a correctness/security bug in this diff. This is a style/clarity optimization rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:58-61` — `findFirstOrThrow` with `id: booking.userId || 0` throws a raw Prisma `P2025` (unhandled 500) for null-`userId` bookings instead of a typed TRPC error.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addGuestsHandler`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. The `|| 0` fallback strongly indicates `booking.userId` can be null/undefined; in that case the query becomes `id: 0`, which will not exist and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (commonly Prisma P2025 / not-found). This exception is not caught or translated into a `TRPCError`, so it would bubble up as an untyped internal error (500) instead of a controlled TRPC response for bookings without a `userId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:80-81` — if every address was dropped by the *blacklist*, the user is told "emails must be unique and valid"; partial blacklist drops are silent.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the `uniqueGuests` array is computed by filtering out (a) emails already in `booking.attendees` and (b) any email present in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. If the filter removes all inputs (`uniqueGuests.length === 0`), the handler throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, which is misleading when the real reason is “all provided emails were blacklisted and/or already attendees” (not uniqueness/validity). Also, when only some emails are blacklisted/already present, they are silently dropped (no per-email feedback), and the mutation proceeds with the remainder. This behavior is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BookingListItem.tsx:194`, `AddGuestsDialog.tsx:93` — `id`/`data-testid` of `add_members`; these are guests, and "members" means team members elsewhere. Rename before tests depend on it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new “additional_guests” action whose internal id is `add_members` (BookingListItem.tsx) and a button with `data-testid="add_members"` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx). This is a naming/semantics concern ("members" vs "guests"), not a verifiable bug, security issue, or correctness defect introduced by the change. Nothing in the diff shows a collision, broken selector, or incorrect behavior caused by this identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:173` — `return { message: "Guests added" }` is hardcoded English and the client ignores it entirely.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler does end with `return { message: "Guests added" };`, which is indeed hardcoded English. However, nothing in the provided diff shows any consumer relying on this message, and the UI added in `AddGuestsDialog` does not read the mutation result at all (it shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` on success). This makes the hardcoded string at most a minor i18n/consistency nit, not a verifiable bug/correctness defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx:2` — imports from its own package barrel `@calcom/ui` while `index.tsx:153` re-exports it. `dynamic()` saves it from a module-eval cycle, but it pulls the whole UI barrel into the chunk, defeating the lazy split.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` the component imports `Button`, `EmailField`, `Icon`, `Tooltip` from `@calcom/ui` (the package barrel). But `packages/ui/index.tsx` now re-exports `MultiEmail` (via `./form/MultiEmailLazy`). This creates a circular dependency path (`MultiEmail` -> `@calcom/ui` barrel -> re-export of `MultiEmailLazy`), and also means the lazily loaded `MultiEmail` chunk will depend on the UI barrel module, which typically drags many unrelated exports into that chunk and undermines the intended code-splitting benefit. This is a verifiable issue introduced by the diff (internal module importing its own barrel after being added to that barrel).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `MultiEmail.tsx:11` reassigns the `value` prop; `:19` uses `key={index}` on a removable list (focus jumps); `:35` sets `required` with no enclosing `<form>`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `MultiEmail` rendering a dynamic, removable list of `EmailField`s where each item uses `key={index}` and items can be removed via `splice(index, 1)`. This is a known real issue in React: using the array index as a key on a list where elements can be inserted/removed causes React to reuse DOM nodes for different items, leading to focus jumps and potentially mismatched input values. The other two points are weaker: `value = value || []` only reassigns the local parameter (doesn’t mutate the parent prop) and `required` without a form typically has no effect, so they’re not clearly defects on their own.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:124-147` — sparse `CalendarEvent`: no `bookerUrl`, `additionalNotes`, `customInputs`, `responses`, `eventTypeId`. New guests get a confirmation missing the booking questions everyone else's copy shows; `bookerUrl`-derived links may emit `undefined/...`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `addGuests.handler.ts` constructs a `CalendarEvent` (`evt`) with a limited set of fields (title/type/description/times/organizer/attendees/etc.), but the proposed finding relies on assumptions about what `AttendeeScheduledEmail`/`OrganizerScheduledEmail`/`formatCalEvent` require (e.g., `bookerUrl`, `customInputs`, `responses`, `eventTypeId`) and how missing fields would affect rendered emails/links. None of those dependencies’ field requirements or link construction are shown in this diff, so the claim that confirmations will miss booking questions or produce `undefined/...` links is not directly verifiable from the changes presented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `handler:138` — recurring: `recurringEvent` is set on `evt` but only one occurrence is modified. UI hides the action on the recurring tab (`BookingListItem.tsx:246`); the API does not.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does set `evt.recurringEvent = parseRecurringEvent(booking.eventType?.recurringEvent)` in `addGuests.handler.ts`, but the finding’s claim that “only one occurrence is modified” (and therefore this is incorrect) depends on how `EventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` interprets `recurringEvent` and what a “booking” represents for recurring event types—neither is shown in the diff. Likewise, the statement that the UI hides this action on a “recurring tab” at `BookingListItem.tsx:246` cannot be verified from the provided diff context (the added menu item is unconditional, and no recurring-specific UI logic is shown). So the finding relies on assumptions outside the diff rather than a directly verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BookingListItem.tsx:357-361` — `AddGuestsDialog` mounted per row. Consistent with existing dialogs, so pre-existing, but compounding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an <AddGuestsDialog> JSX block inside BookingListItem, which is rendered per booking row, but this matches the existing pattern in the same component (other dialogs like EditLocationDialog/ChargeCardDialog are also mounted per row). The finding is primarily a performance/architecture observation rather than a clear, verifiable defect introduced by this change, and there’s no concrete bug shown in the diff stemming from this mounting behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: **Scope vs. title:** "guest *management*" but only add is implemented — no list, edit, or remove. Per C2, no remove means no way to undo an abusive add.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds an “Add Guests” action/dialog and backend mutation, but it does not show anything about the PR title or scope (“guest management”), so a scope-vs-title mismatch is not verifiable from the diff alone. Also, the claim that there is “no way to undo an abusive add” is not provably introduced by this change: the diff does not establish that guest removal/editing is absent elsewhere in the codebase (it simply isn’t part of this diff). This is more of a product completeness suggestion than a concrete defect introduced here.
